record.paper_title: Gamma-ray emitting narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies. New discoveries and open questions
record.context_brief: Modified spin paradigm in spiral-host NLSy1s
record.original_question: Can the modified spin paradigm for relativistic jet production accommodate radio-loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies if these systems are hosted by spiral galaxies: specifically, how can a central supermassive black hole in such a system acquire enough spin for efficient jet production when the paradigm associates high average spin and efficient spin-up with elliptical galaxies and major mergers?

evidence.quote: According to the “modified spin paradigm”, another fundamental parameter for the efficiency of a relativistic jet production should be the BH spin, with SMBHs in elliptical galaxies having on average much larger spins than SMBHs in spiral galaxies.

This is due to the fact that the spiral galaxies are characterized by multiple accretion events with random angular momentum orientation and small increments of mass, while elliptical galaxies undergo at least one major merger with large matter accretion triggering an efficient spin-up of the SMBH.
The accretion rate (thus the mass) and the spin of the BH seem to be related to the host galaxy, leading to the hypothesis that relativistic jets can form only in elliptical galaxy.

Considering also that NLSy1s are thought to be hosted in spiral galaxies, their detection in γ rays poses intriguing questions about the nature of these sources, the production of relativistic jets, the mechanisms of high-energy emission, and the cosmological evolution of radio-loud AGN.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the modified spin paradigm for the production of relativistic jets by accreting supermassive black holes (SMBHs). Under this paradigm:

(i) The efficiency of relativistic jet production depends, in addition to mass and accretion rate, on the dimensionless spin parameter a of the central SMBH.
(ii) SMBHs hosted in elliptical galaxies are predicted to have on average much larger spins than SMBHs hosted in spiral galaxies, because elliptical galaxies are assumed to undergo at least one major merger producing large coherent matter accretion that spins the black hole up to near-extremal values.
(iii) Spiral galaxies are characterized by multiple accretion events with randomly oriented angular momentum and small mass increments, which on average tend to keep the SMBH spin low.
(iv) Consequently, powerful, persistent relativistic jets are predicted to form essentially only in elliptical hosts.

Now consider the empirical class of radio-loud, γ-ray detected narrow-line Seyfert 1 (NLSy1) galaxies, which are observed to launch relativistic jets but are typically hosted by spiral (disk-like) galaxies that have not undergone major mergers.

Problem: Provide a physically consistent extension or modification of the modified spin paradigm above that explains how the SMBH at the center of a spiral-hosted NLSy1 galaxy can acquire and maintain a spin sufficiently high to power the observed relativistic jets, despite the absence of a major merger and the predominance of randomly oriented small accretion events. The proposed mechanism must (a) be quantitatively compatible with the observed jet powers and Lorentz factors of γ-ray NLSy1s, (b) be consistent with the inferred SMBH masses (typically 10^6–10^8 solar masses) and high accretion rates (close to or above the Eddington limit) of these systems, and (c) reproduce the rarity of jetted NLSy1s relative to the parent NLSy1 population.
artifact.category_tag: Relativistic jets and black hole spin
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent observational studies of jetted NLSy1 host galaxies (e.g., comprehensive morphological surveys finding >50 modelled hosts dominated by disks/spirals, and dedicated investigations of individual sources such as 1H 0707-495 and PKS 1502+036) have substantially undermined the strict form of the modified spin paradigm: disk-like galaxies clearly do launch and maintain relativistic jets. Theoretical work on hybrid jet-launching models (combining Blandford-Znajek and Blandford-Payne mechanisms) has been used to reproduce the jet powers of γ-ray NLSy1s without requiring a major-merger spin-up history. However, a fully predictive, quantitatively complete revision of the spin paradigm that explains rarity, jet powers, and host-galaxy demographics simultaneously is not yet established, so the question is best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Jetted narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies breaking the jet paradigm: host-galaxy morphologies
status_evidence.snippet: With >50 modelled hosts of jetted NLS1s, only a few are ellipticals; disk-like galaxies are able to launch and maintain relativistic jets, and the traditional jet paradigm is severely outdated.
status_evidence.claim: Empirical evidence shows spiral/disk hosts can sustain relativistic jets, contradicting the strict spin paradigm.

status_evidence.title: The jet formation mechanism of gamma-ray narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies
status_evidence.snippet: Jet power of almost all gamma-ray NLS1s can be explained by a hybrid Blandford-Znajek + Blandford-Payne model.
status_evidence.claim: Hybrid jet-launching models partially account for jet powers in spiral-hosted NLSy1s.

status_evidence.title: The mass and spin of the extreme NLSy1 1H 0707-495 and implications for the trigger for relativistic jets
status_evidence.snippet: Spin measurements in extreme NLSy1s inform the trigger for relativistic jets.
status_evidence.claim: Direct spin estimates in NLSy1s contribute to revising the spin paradigm.
